text:
lina: Heads-up: proposal to split prober visibility and sample export from the core intake path. Reason: reduce control-plane load and give infra/qa safer, auditable access to probe results. Quick sketch below.

ben: quick question 177 what do you mean by 'split'?

lina: two pieces: (1) a read-only visibility surface (metadata + sample manifests) exposed as a snapshot API; (2) an asynchronous export job that stages sample bundles to signed-object storage. Intake still triggers probes but won't stream raw samples through control plane.

samir: pros/cons: pro: fewer memory spikes on control plane, easier to rate-limit exports. con: slightly more operational complexity (jobs, storage lifecycle).

ash: can we keep small-scale instant reads for UI? i.e., snapshot endpoint returns summary quickly while background job handles full artifact export.

lina: exactly. Snapshot gives counts, seed, last_run_ts, artifact URLs when ready, and a sanitized sample preview (first 3 entries) for quick inspection. Full artifacts are only via export jobs with S3 signed URLs.

ben: auth model: snapshot: onboard:read metadata; preview: onboard:read:preview; full sample downloads: onboard:read:samples. That keeps PII gated.

samir: sampling determinism: include seed + epoch + algorithm name in metadata. We'll use deterministic reservoir sampling seeded by bench-run id so reproducing is straightforward.

ash: runtime routing: annotate prober traffic with X-Prober-Intent=synth|golden|replay so serving can optionally treat it as low-priority and avoid polluting latency SLO telemetry. Need a minimal doc change in routing rules.

ben: metric set for canary: snapshot latency (p50/p95), job queue depth, signed-URL generation latency, artifact download success rate, number of preview hits, and synthetic traffic percentage of total requests.

lina: privacy: add field sanitization_passed (boolean) and a compliance_hash (opaque) in snapshot. If false, preview and exports are blocked for anyone outside model-team.

samir: implementation plan: I'll author v1 JSON contract and webhook payload. Key fields: model_id, run_id, seed, epoch, sample_count, sanitized_preview, artifact_manifest (list of object keys), sanitization_passed, last_run_ts, duration_ms, status. Keep manifest as list of object names (no inline blobs).

ben: I'll prepare a tiny infra consumer lib snippet (python) that polls the snapshot endpoint and kicks off exports via POST /onboard/{model}/exports. Also will add dashboards.

ash: gateway responsibilities: implement scopes, rate-limits per-tenant for preview/download, and quota metrics exported to billing. We'll enforce short-lived signed URLs for artifacts and rsync-friendly export mode for bulk consumers.

qa-bot: smoke-5950012346: quick-smoke passed (samples=120, fails=0) 1 artifact ready: https://s3.redwood/internal/probes/5950012346/preview.json

lina: rollout: feature-flag behind per-tenant opt-in. Phase 1: internal tenants only, webhooks enabled to reduce polling. Phase 2: open snapshot reads to infra + QA. Phase 3: enable export jobs for partners. Monitor for any storage/egress spikes.

ben: one more: how do we handle model reingestion where sample ids collide? Use run_id namespacing (model-run-{ts}) and include stable fingerprint so consumers can detect duplicates.

samir: action items:
- samir: draft v1 snapshot/export JSON and seed spec.
- ben: consumer SDK + canary dashboards.
- ash: scope + quota wiring in gateway.
- lina: RFC blurb + canary tenant list.

lina: timeline: RFC today, prototype next sprint, internal canary after prototype, broader rollout after 2 weeks of canary telemetry. Thanks! :thumbsup:
